question: Should “Only on user action” strictly forbid the intentional background-startup Claude OAuth bootstrap exception, accepting that uncached OAuth may wait until the user opens the menu or refreshes?
rationale: The setting name and reported prompt support the PR’s strict interpretation, but merged release history explicitly preserved the startup exception, so automation cannot safely choose this credential-access and upgrade tradeoff.

options.title: Make the policy strict
options.body: Approve the direction after proof and documentation so background startup never performs an interactive Claude credential read under “Only on user action.”

options.title: Preserve startup bootstrap
options.body: Retain the exception and pursue a narrower mitigation such as a non-interactive preflight, cooldown adjustment, or visible startup consent flow.

recommendation.title: Make the policy strict
recommendation.body: Approve the direction after proof and documentation so background startup never performs an interactive Claude credential read under “Only on user action.”

likelyOwner.reason: They authored and merged the current Claude prompt-policy and adjacent OAuth Keychain behavior.
